title.narrative: ROAP/LA/S1-32QXB-000801 – United Nations Coordinated Technical Assistance to the Government of Lao PDR on Green and Climate Finance

description.narrative: Despite ambitious environmental and climate objectives, Lao PDR remains vulnerable to the impacts of the triple planetary crisis and locked in a growth model dependent on unsustainable natural resource use. Recent economic and financial difficulties have exacerbated the disconnect between Lao PDR’s ambitious environmental policy and resources available to implement this agenda. As recognised by the Government of Lao PDR and development partners at the January 2023 and February 2024 Roundtable Implementation Meetings, economic difficulties have driven Lao PDR “to rely on natural resource extraction as a coping mechanism” – often at the expense of environmental sustainability. Responding to a request from the Ministry of Planning and Investment, the United Nations Joint Programme on Coordinated Technical Assistance on Green and Climate Finance seeks to provide integrated support to addressing policy and resource allocation incoherences through the implementation of chapter 5.3 on “Green and Climate Finance” of the 9th National Socio-Economic Development Plan (NSEDP) Financing Strategy, endorsed by Prime Minister H.E. Sonexay Siphandone in June 2023. As per its theory of change, the joint programme foresees a two-fold approach to support sustainably financing green growth and climate-resilient development: i. enhancing coordination of environmental and broader development planning efforts for greater integration and policy coherence; ii. expanding technical support to address current gaps in policy implementation. Under this joint programme: United Nations Coordinated Technical Assistance to the Government of Lao PDR on Green and Climate Finance, UN-Habitat is responsible for implementing output 2.8 incentivising urban investment in green growth with the aim to strengthen capacity and processes to access climate-friendly finance at the city level, targeting Kaysone Phomvihane and Pakse cities. Activities will include a diagnostic of key challenges in the current green and climate finance environment, the identification of baselines for key Own Source Revenues, the development of guidelines for local-level climate investment, a training workshop on local-level green and climate finance and engagement with a training institute for scaling up and anchoring the capacity building initiative.
